svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: iPadOS · Editor preview page · interval, originals on a device nearby · landscape
svg.desc: Mirrors App/EditorPreviewPage.swift `floatingBody(in:)` — the editor's PREVIEW PAGE on an iPad in LANDSCAPE when a device of this PicPlace account, on the same network, holds the originals (nearby originals, docs/nearby-originals-plan.md §7; Steven's brief of 2026-09-28: 'Preview only · The originals are only on iPhone for now · [Import originals from {Steve iPhone 18}]'); the iPad twin of iOS/project-photo.viewer.preview.nearby.portrait.svg. Everything but the status card is project-photo.viewer.preview.landscape.svg's: `Self.fit(aspect:in:)` sizes the picture to the whole safe area at the poster's aspect and the ZStack seats it top-left — a 3:4 shoot is 582 × 776 at (0, 24), poster.jpg as it is, never graded again — so the taller card moves nothing; `touchChrome` (Back and ⓘ at x 16 / 60, the tab pill trailing at 16 with Editor selected and Text · Frames · Masks locked, amber at 38 %, all centred on y 54); App/EditorControls/EditorGroupBar.swift (`.padPill`, `locked: true`) beside the card, 380 × 66, right 16, bottom 784, cells #8E8E93 at 42 %, none selected, the dots amber at 55 % (Presets, Light). THE OFFER: `NearbyService.offer(for:shortfall:)` (App/Nearby/NearbyService.swift) — a device that answered the holdings question with every original, not busy; a Mac first, else the first to answer (N14) — reaches the card through `PicPlaceController.fetchOffer` as `.nearby(NearbyOffer, alsoOnPicPlace:)`, ahead of PicPlace (N12); the page asks for it on appear (`nearby.want(captureID)`, beside loadHoldings and refreshProject). The card shows it only while that device answers (N7, N15): LetsLapse closed there, or another network, and this is the page's 'not uploaded yet' card again. THE FOOT ROW, HStack(alignment: .bottom, spacing 18) padded 16: `statusCard(style: .dark)` with `CardAction.importNearby` in the editor's timeline-capsule seat (x 16 → 766, `maxWidth: .infinity`). THE CARD: radius 16, black 60 % over .ultraThinMaterial, padding 12, VStack(spacing 10) — the INTERVAL · 54 s · 55 frames badge (App/EditorControls/EditorMarqueeBadge.swift), then HStack(alignment: .top, spacing 10): `StatusGlyphView(.asset(.originals, .nowhere), size 13, surface .photo)` — the slashed camera, white at 45 %: PicPlace doesn't hold them either (with `alsoOnPicPlace` the grey camera stays); the title `ProjectHoldings.Tier.label` 'Preview only' 13 pt semibold white; the caption 11.5 pt #8E8E93 '\(subject) \(verb) only on \(nearby.deviceName) for now' → 'The originals are only on iPhone 18 Pro for now', one line: with the action out of the row the column could take 680 pt (the card less padding, the 18 pt glyph, two 10 pt gaps and the Spacer's 8); then the full-width button under the row, 'Import \(what) from \(deviceName)' → 'Import originals from iPhone 18 Pro' ('the originals' loses its article; a Photo capture reads 'Import the full-size photo from …'), 14 pt semibold black on LL.amber, lineLimit 2, 9 pt above and below the line, radius 10, the card's width less its padding (726). Bottom-aligned with the buttons pill, the card GROWS UP by the button (10 + 34.71): 750 × 130.94, its top at 653.06 (697.77 at rest), over the poster's foot. The press (or a tap on a greyed control, whose prompt reads 'Import the originals from iPhone 18 Pro?' · Import and Continue · Stay as Is) → `PicPlaceController.fetch` → `importNearby`: the same task slot, progress and Stop as a download — the card reads 'Importing the originals' over 'Asking iPhone 18 Pro for the files…', then 'From iPhone 18 Pro · 120 MB of 209,9 MB' with the amber bar, the ↓ cloud and Stop — landing on the Editor page. With `alsoOnPicPlace` the caption reads 'Editing needs the originals — on iPhone 18 Pro nearby, and on PicPlace · 55 files · 209,9 MB' (still one line at this width), the camera grey, the same button. A failed import's sentence (`NearbyService.importErrors`) replaces the caption until the next press. The device's name is `DeviceName.current` on the other device — the model where iOS says only 'iPhone' (N5). GEOMETRY: the iPhone mirror's card offsets carried to this width, and the card laid out headlessly with the code's own modifiers (SwiftUI ImageRenderer on the Mac, 2026-09-28: one-line caption at 256 pt, one-line button label at 237.7 pt centred in 726) — iOS SF Pro metrics for the seats, as the sibling files. Not screenshot-verified on an iPad: the 2026-09-28 bench ran iPhone Simulators. HOOKS: the nearby bench — two Simulators bound to one picplace.test account (`LL_PICPLACE_TOKENS`, one token per install), the originals `LL_REGISTER`ed on the first and the project pulled as a preview on an iPad Simulator in landscape; `LL_DROP_SOURCES=<uuid>:originals` then `LL_TAB=gallery LL_ITEM=<uuid>` there with the first open (`LL_NEARBY_IMPORT=<uuid>` presses the button). iPad PORTRAIT takes `railBody`: the same card, dark (railCardStyle is .dark on iOS, so the badge rides in it too), under the buttons card in the rail — min(340, 42 %) wide, a 308 pt card — undrawn.

g.data-symbol: camera.fill + a slash knocked through (no SF camera.slash)

g.text: The originals are only on iPhone 18 Pro for now
